name: TDC ADMET CYP2D6_Veith
description: Predict whether a compound inhibits the drug-metabolising enzyme cytochrome P450 2D6 (1) or not (0) from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint CYP2D6_Veith of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the area under the precision-recall curve on the test compounds, with class 1 as the positive class, averaged over the five runs; higher is better.
contract: fit_predict(train_smiles, train_y, valid_smiles, valid_y, test_smiles, info) -> sequence of finite numbers, one per test molecule in the given order: a score that is larger for class 1 (for example its probability). train_smiles, valid_smiles and test_smiles are lists of SMILES strings, train_y and valid_y lists of numbers; info has name, metric, kind ('regression' or 'binary') and seed. Score: mean over the seeds 1 to 5 of the area under the precision-recall curve (class 1 positive) on the test part, maximized.
notes: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet
Predicts the binary CYP2D6 inhibition label (1 = inhibitor, from a quantitative high-throughput screen) of 13,130 compounds from their SMILES strings, scored by AUPRC.
Leaders are large tuned ensembles or foundation-model fine-tunes.
Needs PyTDC and rdkit: not in .venv-tasks, so the evaluator restarts itself under tools/venv-admet (created by the README's setup steps).

Every scoring call of the candidate runs in the main suite's sandbox (a child process with an audit hook, 700 s and 6 GB for one call): it keeps a search from coming across the test labels and is not a security boundary against a candidate written to attack the evaluator.
One evaluation of the starting program took 130 s in the run of 2026-11-11, more than the arena's default limit of 120 s: raise AR_EVAL_TIMEOUT for this task.

science_relevance.reason: Veith et al. measured the inhibition of these isozymes by thousands of compounds, which is the property the task predicts; the paper's main objective is the characterisation of isozyme inhibition.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Classify molecules as inhibitors or non-inhibitors of the cytochrome P450 isozyme CYP2D6 from their structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: CYP2D6 is one of the main drug-metabolising enzymes; its inhibition by a co-administered drug raises the exposure of other drugs and causes drug-drug interactions, so inhibition is screened for early.

papers.title: Comprehensive characterization of cytochrome P450 isozyme selectivity across chemical libraries
papers.task_relation: The task predicts, from structure, the inhibition label of the isozyme named in the task, which this screen measured for about 12,000 compounds; the paper's own aim is the measurement, not a predictor, and the local split and metric are different.
papers.primary_goal: Measure the inhibition of five major cytochrome P450 isozymes by about 17,000 compounds in a quantitative high-throughput screen and characterise isozyme selectivity.
